newsitem.title: USA: Manufacturing activity up in April - KC Fed survey.
newsitem.headline: Manufacturing activity up in April - KC Fed survey.

text.p: Manufacturing activity in the 10th U.S. economic district rose slightly in April from January, with manufacturers showing optimism about the near-future outlook, a quarterly survey by the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City showed.
"Manufacturers were optimistic about the outlook for the next six months," William Keeton, a senior economist at the Kansas City Fed and author of the survey, said in a statement.
The highlights of the study showed inventories as well as manufacturing employment edged up in April. Prices for raw materials increased slightly faster than January.

District manufacturers were positive about the near-term outlook, though not as quite upbeat as in the last survey. "Indexes of activity expected in the next six months continue to signal expansion," Keeton said.
Here follows a breakdown of the components of the survey for the 10th District Manufacturing Conditions for April.*
* The survey takes a snapshot of manufacturing during the first month of each quarter by asking plant managers about a variety of indicators.
The diffusion index was calculated by subtracting the percentage of total respondents reporting decreases in a given indicator from the percentage of those reporting increases.
Index values greater than zero generally suggest expansion, while values less than zero indicate contraction.
The closer index values are to 100, the more widespread are increases among respondents. The closer it is to -100, the more widespread are decreases.
The April survey included 204 responses from plants in the Tenth Federal Reserve District's seven states.
